My conclusion is still A. In a lien theory state, the majority view is that one joint tenant's mortgage is only a lien on that tenant's interest and doesn't sever the joint tenancy, so the lien dies with him and the survivor takes the whole property. Your note says the key is B or C, but both conflict with the majority rule, since C describes title theory and B isn't a real requirement. If you have to choose between those two, C is the closer fit, but I think the key may be wrong.

CONFIDENCE: 60
